text.p: Unseeded Andrei Chesnokov of Russia suffered a horrifying multiple fracture of his lower right leg Tuesday during a first-round match against Australian Todd Woodbridge at the Advanta Championships.
The 69th-ranked Chesnokov, 31, broke his tibia and fibula and dislocated the ankle. He was taken to a local hospital by ambulance and was scheduled to have surgery Wednesday.
The 26th-ranked Woodbridge was leading Chesnokov 6-3 1-0, 40-15 when the accident occurred. Chesnokov had just scrambled to hit a backhand when he fell to the ground.
"It was a horrible, horrible incident," Woodbridge said. "It's a shock seeing something like that. I've never seen anyone do something like that. It was like seeing a bad car accident."
"It's the worst injury I've seen in tennis," said ATP Tour trainer Doug Spreen. "It's not a career-threatening type of injury, but I think he'll be out a minimum of four to six months."

"I just heard this enormous crack," Woodbridge said. "For a moment or two he didn't scream, but then he just screamed, blood-curdling screams. It just wanted to make you throw up. I'm surprised he was not passed out."
